findings.title: Release test timeout was shorter than its one-hour contract
findings.original_evidence: tests/test_verify_test_suite_timeout.py expected 3600 seconds and observed 1800
findings.proposed_fix: Use a 3600-second timeout per release suite.
findings.retest_evidence: 3 Sep 2026, isolated worktree retest/f500-003 off origin/main@2f7fdc5c, commit 5f88acd1 (TEST_SUITE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS 1800->3600 only - an unrelated gate_nav_verified 'unmeasured'-handling change found bundled into the same uncommitted diff in the shared worktree was deliberately excluded as out of this finding's scope). Regression test confirmed the defect first: tests/test_verify_test_suite_timeout.py failed pre-fix (assert all(timeout==3600...) -> False), passed post-fix (1/1). Root cause of the regression traced one level: an earlier fix (commit b465bd1f, 28 Aug 2026) had already set this constant to 3600 with the same regression test, but candidate_base 2f7fdc5c carries 1800 again - lost via a merge, not re-investigated further here. SECOND closure test ('Full database-backed verifier', i.e. `python scripts/verify.py --gate tests --require-db`) could NOT be completed in this session: three attempts (two backgrounded run_in_background invocations and one direct redirect-to-file invocation, each 40-90+ minutes) all terminated at the harness/shell level (empty output files, exit 127 or 255) rather than at the test level - `tasklist` confirmed genuine pytest worker processes alive and consuming 800MB-1.8GB RAM mid-run each time, so this reads as a session/background-duration ceiling in the interactive tool harness on this Windows host, not a defect in the fix or a test failure. Recommend rerunning `python scripts/verify.py --require-db` (or just `--gate tests --require-db`) either in CI or as a detached, non-interactively-monitored process with a longer-lived shell before marking this verified - do not treat the unit-level pass alone as satisfying both named closure tests.

findings.title: .gitignore blanket-ignores scripts/check_*.py, requiring a manual allowlist line per permanent gate - the likely root mechanism behind F500-008
findings.original_evidence: 3 Sep 2026, worktree gov-gates (branch feat/docs-drift-and-check-registration, base e74bd8ec): creating two new checker scripts (scripts/check_docs_drift.py, scripts/check_unregistered_checks.py) and running `git add` showed 'The following paths are ignored by one of your .gitignore files'. `git check-ignore -v` traced both to .gitignore:196 `scripts/check_*.py`. The surrounding comment already documents one prior casualty: 'these globs are why DESIGN.md can reference a check_token_migration.py pre-commit hook that is absent from the repository - a permanent quality gate was named like a throwaway and got ignored out of existence.' Every one of the 70 check_*.py scripts currently tracked required its own `!scripts/check_X.py` negation line added by hand; the default is to silently drop a new one unless the author notices and force-adds it.
findings.required_fix: This finding was fixed rather than left open, since it was a one-line addition needed anyway to commit the two new gates: negation lines added for both new scripts. The systemic direction (default-ignore + manual allowlist for a class of file meant to be permanent) is unchanged and worth inverting - default-track scripts/check_*.py and ignore only files matching a genuinely-scratch naming convention (scripts/check_*_scratch.py, or similar) - but that broader change is out of scope of this fix and not attempted here.
findings.retest_evidence: 3 Sep 2026: both new scripts committed successfully after the negation lines were added (commit 037490fc); `git ls-files scripts/check_*.py | wc -l` -> 72 (70 pre-existing + 2 new), confirming both are now tracked.
closure_tests: git check-ignore -v scripts/check_docs_drift.py scripts/check_unregistered_checks.py must report no match
git ls-files scripts/check_*.py includes both new scripts

findings.title: Firefox console diagnostics collapsed structured errors to the word Object
findings.original_evidence: Exact-SHA Firefox job in CI run 33804483255 failed the 320px motivation repository check with only `Motivation repository raised JavaScript errors: ['Object']`. Diagnostic run 33807384189 reproduced the same opaque plain-object page error at 768px, proving it arrived through Playwright's pageerror channel rather than console and still lost the thrown object's fields.
findings.required_fix: Serialize every console argument with source location, preserve page-error stacks, and install a pre-page error/unhandled-rejection probe that copies every exception into a fresh serializable diagnostic record before Firefox discards its fields.
findings.retest_evidence: Exact-SHA run 33808606132 again failed Linux Firefox with three opaque Object page errors, while its Chromium and WebKit jobs passed. Run 33810262875 then passed 55/56: the failure moved to BusinessProcess while all motivation viewports passed, and every page/API request returned 200. The first enhanced probe emitted nothing because Playwright had been given an uninvoked arrow expression; a runtime contract reproduced that absence before the probe was corrected to an IIFE. The corrected probe reproduced the failure locally on Equipment and retained the exact object: `{isFromCancelledTransition: true}`, Alpine's documented internal sentinel when one visual transition supersedes another. Archie's production error handler already prevents and ignores that exact benign signal; Playwright Firefox surfaced it before the later handler could prevent the harness pageerror. A failing-before/passing-after browser contract now makes the earliest qualification listener prevent only that exact sentinel, while an independent contract proves other plain-object rejections remain serialized and release-blocking. Seven diagnostic contracts pass locally. The complete exact 56-case Firefox compatibility command then passed 56/56 in 392.93 seconds on the corrected branch, including Equipment, BusinessProcess and all motivation viewports. Final Linux Firefox CI remains authoritative.

findings.title: Export-recovery contract raced a 150-millisecond database lease
findings.original_evidence: Exact-SHA PostgreSQL 16 CI run 33810262875: test_premature_export_recovery_remains_retryable_after_database_lease_expiry expected a pre-expiry RuntimeError, but setup and session work consumed its 150ms lease, so production correctly treated the already-expired lease as recoverable.
findings.required_fix: Use a comfortably long initial lease for the pre-expiry ownership assertion, then cross the durable boundary explicitly by updating dispatch_lease_expires_at relative to the database clock before testing recovery; do not use wall-clock sleeps.
findings.retest_evidence: 4 Sep 2026: the corrected test passed inside a 13/13 combined root retest. The implementation uses a 30-second initial lease and an organization-scoped SQL update to set the persisted expiry to clock_timestamp() minus one second. No production code changed. Exact-SHA PostgreSQL 16 CI run 33831735604 then passed all 3,992 tests with zero skips or expected failures.
closure_tests: Full non-smoke CI suite on final SHA

findings.title: Default ArchiMate viewpoint performs a duplicate initial render
findings.original_evidence: Exact-SHA Linux Firefox run 33830528607 failed three motivation-responsive viewports with an opaque object exception. Prior diagnostic reproduction retained Alpine's `{isFromCancelledTransition: true}` sentinel, and request evidence repeatedly showed two identical initial layer-element calls. Source tracing found dashboard init loads elements immediately, then reloads after the default Basic/All Elements viewpoint resolves even though its intentionally empty element_types array adds no filter.
findings.required_fix: Do not repeat the initial element request when the resolved viewpoint has no type filter; retain the refresh when a non-empty viewpoint filter changes the requested data.
findings.retest_evidence: 4 Sep 2026 strict runtime TDD: the real dashboard.js component factory produced two unfiltered requests before the fix (`[null, null]`, test red) while the non-empty viewpoint case produced the required filtered refresh. After requiring a non-empty element_types array, the runtime test observes one default request and two requests only for the filtered case. The focused dashboard/repository suite passed 11/11. Exact-SHA Linux CI run 33831735604 then passed all 56 Firefox checks, including all three formerly failing responsive viewports.

findings.title: Immutable-image audit omitted the optional email worker from resolved Compose
findings.original_evidence: Exact-SHA CI run 33831735604 passed every application, browser, database, security and dependency job, then release job 100901957263 failed before image publication with KeyError: 'worker'. The worker is intentionally declared under the disabled-by-default email Compose profile, so an ordinary `compose config` omitted it while the audit still attempted to inspect it.
findings.required_fix: Resolve production Compose with the email profile enabled during the immutable-image audit. This must inspect both active and dormant application services without enabling the worker in production.
findings.retest_evidence: 4 Sep 2026 strict TDD: the release-artifact contract failed until the CI command explicitly included `--profile email`; the corrected contract passed 5/5, the merged main/release cohort passed 37/37, and the merged static verifier passed 44/44 with zero skips. Exact-SHA release-image execution remains pending.
